title: Even-Dimensional Spectral Uniformity of the Inverse Permutation
summary: An odd-dimensional bound is known, but its proof does not extend to even dimensions; prove or refute the conjectured spectral-uniformity value for the inverse permutation.

formal_statement.body: For even $n$, prove or refute that the inverse permutation on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ has spectral uniformity $2^{n/2}+2$. A bound is established for the inverse function when $n$ is odd, but that proof does not cover even $n$, where the inverse function is not APN; thus the stated value remains a conjectured target for the even-dimensional case.

scope.domain: This is a structural question in symmetric cryptography and vectorial Boolean-function theory about the spectral uniformity of an inverse permutation over a binary vector space.
parameters: n, the dimension of the binary vector space
spectral uniformity, the quantity being evaluated
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute the stated spectral-uniformity value for the inverse permutation when n is even; the available odd-dimensional bound does not settle this case.

progress.summary: The source reports a bound for the inverse function when n is odd, but says the proof does not cover even n, where the inverse is not APN. It presents the even-dimensional spectral-uniformity value as a conjecture based on numerical experiments.
